information_and_model_claim.modeling_question: Can training-only positive-redundancy balancing stop a large family of similar favorable percentile factors from dominating a complete-library consensus without using return targets or deleting any factor?
information_and_model_claim.historical_policy_permission: A complete-library historical combination remains allowed when the transform, finite graph rule, aggregation, support and every gate are frozen before component values, scores or returns.

nearest_consumed_families.family: Campaign044 and later feature-equal arithmetic consensus
nearest_consumed_families.reason: A feature-equal mean gives total weight proportional to the number of features in a redundant family. Campaign134 gives every connected redundancy component equal total weight, so two libraries with identical feature mean but different correlation-component membership can produce different scores.
Campaign134 never selects an order statistic or lower tail. It retains all 140 values and changes only the frozen positive weight assigned through training-only redundancy components.

Campaign134 never reads a target when defining components or weights. Its weights are a closed-form function of positive feature correlation and component sizes; there is no loss, penalty, coefficient bound or return-fit optimization.
Campaign134 uses current favorable percentile levels and training-window cross-feature redundancy. It does not compare each factor with its prior-session rank or count directional improvement signs.

nearest_consumed_families.family: Campaign132 trees and Campaign133 marginal PAVA
nearest_consumed_families.reason: There are no targets, trees, interactions, marginal response levels or prior model scores. The terminal Campaign132/133 binaries and scores are never inputs.

nearest_consumed_families.family: PCA, covariance optimization and supervised cluster ensembles
nearest_consumed_families.reason: The sole admitted graph has one fixed +0.8 edge boundary and connected-component rule; no component count, linkage, covariance shrinkage, objective, negative weight, target weight or cluster selection is searched.

algebraic_and_counterfactual_checks: If all 140 features form singleton components, Campaign134 reduces exactly to the feature-equal arithmetic mean; if any multi-feature component exists, its family receives exactly one component share rather than one share per member.
Every source factor always has strictly positive weight 1/(component_count*component_size); no training correlation outcome can delete, invert or duplicate a factor.

Changing a training return cannot change any component or score because returns are absent from graph fitting; changing a validation return cannot change the already written validation score or uniqueness record.

Permuting factor order together with feature identities preserves connected-component membership and the arithmetic result, while the frozen order only determines deterministic component/member serialization.
Changing Candidate49, current daily data, a provider credential or the 2024-2025 lockbox cannot change Campaign134's training graph or historical score.

admission.reason: This is a finite unsupervised redundancy-allocation mechanism rather than a refreshed target fit or a new order statistic.
